title: cerastium arvense subsp. thomasii
intro: Cerastium arvense subsp. thomasii, commonly known as a wild candytuft, is a flowering plant species native to Europe. It is used in traditional medicine to support various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, which can aid in wound healing, reduce fever, and combat infections. The bioactive constituents of Cerastium arvense subsp. thomasii include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and triterpenes, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, promote tissue repair, and exhibit antimicrobial activity, making it a valuable resource in traditional medicine.
